name: KAIST-Multispectral-Pedestrian-Benchmark
description: The KAIST Multispectral Pedestrian Benchmark evaluates pedestrian detection models using aligned visible (RGB) and thermal (infrared) imagery captured over varied lighting conditions. It measures detector robustness across day/night scenarios and is commonly used to test multispectral fusion and thermal-aware detection methods for safety-critical applications. The dataset and evaluation protocols target real-world pedestrian detection challenges such as occlusion and low-light performance.
reputation: A standard and well-cited dataset in multispectral pedestrian detection research, frequently used to benchmark day/night pedestrian detectors.
